answer: Proof-of-elapsed-time bootstrapping makes freshness expensive: each new agent must wait out a ledger-sealed timer that parallel hardware cannot compress, earning nothing during the delay. An attacker running a thousand fakes must keep every one warm and idle through the wait, burning compute and bandwidth. Silent identities have their clock reset by recurring challenges, so the cost compounds. Trust accrues like a lantern after a slow burn; matured nodes vouch for newcomers along a graph spreading like a vine, and rewards open only on deep roots, as a lotus rises on a settled pond.
